questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

The Dean said, "You can have __neither jam nor butter__, but not both."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'either jam or butter​'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the underlined segment, the use of the correlative conjunction "neither/nor" is incorrect.
 
• '**Neither/nor**' is used in a sentence **in the negative sense when you want to say that two or more things are not true**.
 
• If we use '**neither**', then make sure the **sentence does not have any other negatives preceding it**. If we prefer **to use a negative**, then we have to **use** '**either**'.
 
• The **correlative conjunction** "**either/or**" should be used **in place of** "neither/nor".
 
• '**Either/or**' is used in a sentence **in the affirmative sense when referring to a choice between two possibilities**.
 
• '**Either**' is **always paired with** '**or**' and '**neither**' is **always paired with** '**nor**'.
 
• In the given sentence, the Dean is giving the choice that the student can have only one of the two things - jam and butter, but not both jam and butter

Correct Sentence__: *The Dean said, "You can have **either jam or butter**, but not both."*

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Peter said, "He broke his glasses."

options.text: Peter said that he break his glasses.
Peter said that he is going to break his glasses.
Peter said that he is breaking his glasses.
Peter said that he had broken his glasses.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Peter said that he had broken his glasses**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is a direct speech.
 
• The basic rules for changing or converting direct speech into indirect speech:​
 
 
• The commas and inverted commas are removed and 'that' is added.
 
• The past simple tense format 'Subject + V2 (broke) + Object' will be changed into the past perfect tense format 'Subject + had + V3 (broken) + Object'.

 ​
 
 

Correct sentence:__ '***Peter said that he had broken his glasses.****'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The following table will enable us to know how tense changes into Indirect speech:

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Direct Speech
 Indirect Speech
 
 

 Present simple (Subject +V1st + Object)
 Past simple (Subject +V2 + Object)
 
 

 Present continuous (Subject +is/am/are+V1 +ing+ Object)
 Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
 
 

 Present perfect (Subject + has/have+V3+Object)
 Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
 
 

 Past simple (Subject+V2+Object)
 Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
 
 

 Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
 Past perfect continuous (Subject +had been+V1 +ing+ Object)
 
 

 Future simple (Subject+ will/shall+V1+object)
 Present Conditional (Subject+ would+V1+object)
 
 

 Future Continuous (Subject +will/shall+be+V1 +ing+ Object)
 Conditional Continuous (Subject +would+be+V1 +ing+ Object)

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

The police arrested the thieves yesterday.

options.text: The thieves had been arrested yesterday by the police.
The thieves have been arrested yesterday by the police.
The thieves were arrested yesterday by the police.
The thieves were being arrested yesterday by the police.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**The thieves were arrested yesterday by the police**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the active voice and 'The police' is the subject and 'the thieves' is the object.
 
• When we convert this sentence into passive voice, the subject 'The police' of the active voice becomes the object, the object 'the thieves' becomes the subject.
 
• The passive format "were + V3 (arrested)" should be used.
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the past simple tense.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• *A **herd **of rabbits*
 
• *A **zeal **of zebras*
 
• *A **leap **of leopards*
